findings_verified_by_driver.detail: KitRangePathsQuery::cachedHandle() wraps Cache::remember with a 5-min TTL (3s under impersonation); KitScanPathsQuery::countPoints()/encodedPaths() go straight to filteredQuery() with NO cache. So the endpoint lost its cached read path AND the uncached path widened from GPS-less kits to all kits. Real perf regression. NOT fixed: adding a cache to the scan path is new work, not part of a revert (tier 2 was never cached pre-change either).

The lanes framed this as '15_days/30_days now emit fully undecimated points'. Verified WRONG in mechanism: kit_scan_paths NEVER accepted dedup_meters, so tier 2 was ALWAYS undecimated. What actually changed is that tier 2 now serves ALL kits instead of only GPS-less ones. The volume consequence is real; the 'lost decimation' framing is not.

ac.item: Kit Path Map builds paths from scan data only
ac.evidence: Proven three independent ways. (1) Browser A1: kit 16 — seeded with BOTH sources at deliberately different coordinates — rendered Indianapolis [-86.149,39.7606] with ZERO Austin coords anywhere in the pass. (2) B2: KitScanPathsQuery executed directly returned 60 points / 12 buckets with path_json [[-86.129,39.7806],...]. (3) A4: date_toggles arms verified across 7/15/30 days (2/4/6 rows, trip_dates 08-30 / +08-19 / +08-11). A3 confirms the surviving scan path renders normally. PRODUCTION CARDINALITY (read-only): of 5,570 kits, 611 hold both sources and keep rendering from scan data, 487 are scan-only and unaffected, and exactly 1 renders nothing at 30 days (0 at 7d/15d).

ac.item: No dependency on unavailable merged SC_POSITIONS/kit data for path rendering
ac.evidence: B3 static assertion: KitRangePathsQuery (line 26) and sc_positions (line 23) appear ONLY inside the class docblock — no executable reference. Runtime: kit 17 (45 sc_positions rows, zero scan buckets) returns 200 with [] rather than falling back to GPS (A2, A8); a mixed 3-kit selection contributes nothing for it without failing wholesale (A7). PRODUCTION CARDINALITY: the sole GPS-with-no-scans kit (13075) renders empty rather than falling back to GPS.
